title: Long fingerless gauntlets
subtitle: Extended fingerless mitts reaching the elbow, worked in DK ribbing in the round.
excerpt: Long fingerless gauntlets in DK wool, worked in 2x2 rib in the round from wrist to elbow. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm, with a length of about 30 cm.
sourceNotes: Long ribbed gauntlets and arm warmers appear in Weldon's Practical Knitter from the 1880s onwards, and in Beeton's Book of Needlework (1870). The extended ribbed arm warmer is one of the staple patterns of the Victorian knitting canon, now out of UK and EU copyright.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 30 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in 2x2 rib slightly stretched on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm. Length 30 cm from cast-on to finger edge.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the knitting, then returning to them after the body is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Long fingerless gauntlets in DK wool, worked in 2x2 rib in the round from the finger edge to the elbow, with an
afterthought thumb
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm. Length is 30 cm.
Gauntlets are worked from the finger edge downward so the cast-on sits at the finger and the bind-off at the elbow. The rib grips the arm without needing shaping. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular throughout. Budget about 120 g (265 m / 290 yards) of DK wool for the pair.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 120 g (about 265 m / 290 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 2: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for thumb position

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 30 rounds to 10 cm in 2x2 rib slightly stretched on 3.75 mm needles. At 30 cm finished length, row gauge matters: check both stitch and row gauge before starting.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and finger edge
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 8 rounds of 2x2 rib.
Thumb position

Work the first 10 (11, 12) stitches with waste yarn in rib pattern. Slip back and work in rib to end. Continue in 2x2 rib for 82 (86, 90) more rounds. Total length from cast-on: about 30 cm. Bind off in rib.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn and pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches above and 10 (11, 12) stitches below the gap. Work 12 (14, 14) rounds of 2x2 rib. Bind off in rib.
Adjust the length

Measure from your wrist bone to your elbow. Work the rib section until the gauntlet reaches that length before binding off. The round count given (82 to 90) is a guide for an average 30 cm arm length.
Common faults
Gauntlet twists on the arm: the 2x2 rib spirals slightly as it is worked in the round. This is normal in rib; it will not show when worn.

Bind-off too tight at the elbow: the standard bind-off constricts rib. Use a stretchy bind-off such as working each pair of stitches together before binding off, or use needles two sizes larger for the bind-off row.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry along the full 30 cm length.
What to try next
A cable column running the full length of the gauntlet gives the same wrist-to-elbow coverage with more texture. The cabled fingerless mitts pattern uses the same DK gauge and needle size.
